issues.legal_issue: The restriction on assignment of land acquired through statutory tenant-purchase provisions includes testamentary dispositions.
material_facts: The land had been acquired by a cultivating tenant through the statutory tenant-purchase scheme.
The tenant bequeathed the land by will to a person who was not an agriculturist.
The required prior approval for the disposition had not been obtained.
issues.conclusion: The restriction on transfer of land acquired through the statutory tenant-purchase scheme applies to a testamentary disposition; without the required prior approval, the disposition is invalid.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed the restriction on transfer, including assignment, in light of the statutory scheme granting ownership to cultivating tenants and requiring purchasers to comply with obligations such as personal cultivation. It relied on Sangappa Kalyanappa Bangi v. Land Tribunal, Jamkhandi, Jayamma v. Maria Bai, and Bhavarlal Labhchand Shah v. Kanaiyalal Nathalal Intawala, and held Mahadeo v. Shakuntalabai incorrectly decided because it had not considered the earlier decisions and was inconsistent with the applicable principles. The restriction and its invalidity consequence are set out in Sections 43(1) and 43(2) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 as applicable in Gujarat.

rule.if: agricultural_tenancy_appeal and statutory_purchase_land and testamentary_bequest and approval_not_obtained

predicates.agricultural_tenancy_appeal: The dispute reached the reviewing court through an appeal concerning restrictions on dispositions of agricultural land under a tenancy statute.
predicates.statutory_purchase_land: A tenant acquired the land through a statutory scheme that conferred ownership on cultivating tenants.
predicates.testamentary_bequest: The holder of the land made a will bequeathing it to another person.
predicates.approval_not_obtained: The required prior approval for the disposition had not been obtained.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns land acquired by a tenant through a statutory purchase scheme, a bequest made without required prior approval requires that approval.

issues.legal_issue: The bar on specified transfers of agricultural land in favour of ineligible persons applies to testamentary dispositions.
material_facts: The holder of agricultural land bequeathed it by will to a person who was not an agriculturist.
The required permission for the disposition had not been obtained.
The dispute concerned whether the statutory restrictions on transfers applied to a bequest taking effect after the holder's death.
issues.conclusion: The statutory bar on transfers of agricultural land to a non-agriculturist applies to a testamentary disposition, subject to the statutory permission mechanism.
issues.legal_principle: The court adopted a purposive construction of the transfer restrictions, considering the statutory objective of preserving agricultural land for cultivation and preventing the scheme protecting cultivating tenants from being defeated by bequests to ineligible persons. It relied on Sangappa Kalyanappa Bangi v. Land Tribunal, Jamkhandi, Jayamma v. Maria Bai, Amar Singh v. State of Punjab, and Dayandeo Ganpat Jadhav v. Madhav Vithal Bhaskar, and agreed with the High Court's interpretation of Section 63 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 as applicable in Gujarat. It distinguished decisions concerning testamentary devolution where no statutory prohibition on such a disposition was involved, including State of West Bengal v. Kailash Chandra Kapur and S. Rathinam v. L.S. Mariappan.

rule.if: agricultural_tenancy_appeal and agricultural_land and testamentary_bequest and beneficiary_not_eligible and permission_not_obtained

predicates.agricultural_tenancy_appeal: The dispute reached the reviewing court through an appeal concerning statutory restrictions on agricultural land dispositions.
predicates.agricultural_land: The property at issue was agricultural land.
predicates.testamentary_bequest: The holder of the land made a will bequeathing it to another person.
predicates.beneficiary_not_eligible: The beneficiary did not meet the statutory eligibility requirements for receiving the land.
predicates.permission_not_obtained: The required permission for the disposition had not been obtained.

issues.definition: A bequest of agricultural land to a beneficiary who does not meet the statutory eligibility requirements and has no required permission is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A state restriction on dispositions of agricultural land is not invalid merely because it affects testamentary succession governed by central legislation when its substance concerns the state's authority over agricultural land.
material_facts: The appellants argued that the state restrictions were inconsistent with principles of the central succession legislation and were invalid without presidential assent.
The restrictions governed transfers and alienation of agricultural land and formed part of a scheme protecting cultivating tenants and regulating agricultural holdings.
The effect on testamentary succession arose from applying those land-transfer restrictions to wills.
issues.conclusion: The challenge based on legislative competence and inconsistency with central succession legislation was rejected; the state restrictions remained valid.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the pith-and-substance doctrine, the principle that legislative entries receive a broad construction, and the rule that incidental encroachment on another legislative field does not invalidate an enactment within the state's competence. It relied on Lingappa Pochanna Appelwar v. State of Maharashtra, Welfare Association, A.R.P. v. Ranjit P. Gohil, Girnar Traders (3) v. State of Maharashtra, and the principles on constitutional interpretation cited in those decisions. The court treated regulation of agricultural land transfers as within the state's legislative field concerning land and held that any effect on testamentary succession did not invalidate the restrictions.

predicates.legislative_competence_challenge_in_appe: An appeal included a challenge to the state's authority to enact the land-transfer restriction.
predicates.state_rule_targets_agricultural_land_tra: The challenged state rule principally addressed transfers and alienation of agricultural land.
predicates.central_succession_law_invoked: A party relied on central succession legislation to argue that the state restriction was invalid.
predicates.succession_effect_is_incidental: The restriction affected testamentary succession as a consequence of regulating agricultural land transfers.

issues.definition: A state restriction principally regulating agricultural land transfers remains within the state's legislative competence when its effect on testamentary succession is incidental.
